reason: The after-meal pancreatic cells contain insulin and can release it into the nearby blood, which is the first part of the muscle-storage goal.
expectation: Insulin will be released into the blood.

reaction: The blood route makes the connection between the pancreas and muscle clearer.
reason: The muscle fibres have insulin receptors and glucose nearby, matching the muscle-storage goal.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin will help the muscle fibres take in and store glucose.

effect: Insulin helped muscle store glucose as carbohydrate while remaining outside the cells. The remaining goal is to release liver glucose between meals.
reaction: It is helpful to see the message kept separate from the stored material.
reason: The between-meal pancreatic cells contain glucagon, the named message for releasing liver glucose, and can release it into blood.
expectation: Glucagon will enter the blood and be available to signal the liver.

effect: Glucagon is now in the blood and can carry the between-meal message to the liver.
reaction: The contrast with insulin makes the two messages easier to follow.
reason: The liver carbohydrate store contains the glucose units, and glucagon is the named signal to release them.
expectation: The liver will break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver store released glucose into the blood, completing the between-meal goal. The result also showed that the release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the stored glucose return to the blood.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing glucose in the liver and then releasing it made the contrast between meals and the time between them clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing each pancreatic message into blood felt a little repetitive, although it showed how the messages travel.

surprise.text: The muscle stored glucose while insulin stayed outside the cells; the message was not part of the stored material.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the pictures and goals named the signals and where they needed to go. I followed those hints rather than knowing the detailed mechanism.

continue.text: I would probably try another chapter: seeing the stored glucose released connected the separate steps to a useful body function, though the repeated message-release actions were less engaging.
